q-134531.name: Question 1
q-134531.problem: Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of $(1.02)^{7}$ using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{7}$ in ascending powers of $x.$ Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.
q-134531.worked_solution:
Recall that when $n$ is a positive integer, 

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{1}{2!}n(n-1){x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+x)}^{7} & =1+7x+\frac{1}{2!}\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot {x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n} \\  & =1+7x+21{x}^{2}+⋯+{x}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, for small $x,$ we have

$$
{(1+x)}^{7}≈1+7x+21{x}^{2}.
$$

Now, we substitute $x=0.02$ into the above approximation of $(1+x)^{7}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(1.02)^{7} & =(1+0.02)^{7} \\  & ≈1+7(0.02)+21(0.02)^{2} \\  & =1+7(0.02)+21(0.000\,4) \\  & =1+0.14+0.008\,4 \\  & =1.148\,4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}%\,error & =\frac{\text{amount of error}}{\text{exact value}}\times 100 \\  & =\frac{|(1.02)^{7}-1.148\,4|}{(1.02)^{7}}\times 100 \\  & ≈0.02%\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to two decimal places.

q-134531.html:
Question 1
?

Calculate the percentage error obtained when approximating the value of (1.02)7 using the first three terms of the binomial expansion of (1+x)7 in ascending powers of x. Round your final percentage error to two decimal places.

a
0.07%
b
0.01%
c
0.05%
d
0.02%
e
0.03%
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that when n is a positive integer,

(1+x)n=1+nx+12!n(n−1)x2+⋯+xn.

Therefore,

(1+x)7=1+7x+12!⋅7⋅6⋅x2+⋯+xn=1+7x+21x2+⋯+xn.

So, for small x, we have (1+x)7≈1+7x+21x2.

Now, we substitute x=0.02 into the above approximation of (1+x)7: (1.02)7=(1+0.02)7≈1+7(0.02)+21(0.02)2=1+7(0.02)+21(0.0004)=1+0.14+0.0084=1.1484

Finally, using a calculator, we can compute the percentage error, as follows: %error=amount of errorexact value×100=|(1.02)7−1.1484|(1.02)7×100≈0.02% rounded to two decimal places.

q-134611.html:
Question 2
?

Use the first four terms of the binomial expansion of (1+x)6 in ascending powers of x to approximate (0.84)6. Give your answer to five decimal places.

a
0.34223
b
0.34245
c
0.34208
d
0.35130
e
0.34923
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that when n is a positive integer,

(1+x)n=1+nx+12!n(n−1)x2+13!n(n−1)(n−2)x3+⋯+xn.

Therefore,

(1+x)6=1+6x+12⋅6⋅5⋅x2+16⋅6⋅5⋅4⋅x3+⋯+x6=1+6x+15x2+20x3+⋯+x6.

So, for small x, we have

(1+x)6≈1+6x+15x2+20x3.

Finally, we substitute x=−0.16 into the above approximation of (1+x)6:

(0.84)6=(1+(−0.16))6≈1+6(−0.16)+15(−0.16)2+20(−0.16)3=1−6(0.16)+15(0.0256)−20(0.004096)=1−0.96+0.384−0.08192=0.34208,

to five decimal places.

EXPLANATION

Recall that when n is a positive integer, (1+x)n=1+nx+12!n(n−1)x2+13!n(n−1)(n−2)x3+⋯+xn.

Therefore, (1+x)9=1+9x+12⋅9⋅8⋅x2+16⋅9⋅8⋅7⋅x3+⋯+x9=1+9x+36x2+84x3+⋯+x9.

So, for small x, we have (1+x)9≈1+9x+36x2+84x3.

Finally, we substitute x=−0.08 into the above approximation of (1+x)9: (0.92)9=(1+(−0.08))9≈1+9(−0.08)+36(−0.08)2+84(−0.08)3=1−9(0.08)+36(0.0064)−84(0.000512)=1−0.72+0.2304−0.043008≈0.467 rounded to three decimal places.
